Aries, E., Gómez Benavides, J., Mavromatis, S., Klein, G., Chronopoulos, G. and Roudier, S. (2022). Best Available Techniques (BAT) Reference Document for the Ferrous Metals Processing Industry. Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU (Integrated Pollution Prevention and Control). JRC Science for Policy Report JRC131649, EUR 31321 EN. Publications Office of the European Union, Luxembourg. ISBN 978-92-76-59143-6, doi:10.2760/196475.

Targeted pass of an 852-page BREF. Locators are PRINTED page numbers (PDF page = printed + 6). Main file: EU FMP data-collection (2018, yearly averages 2014-2016) specific energy consumption ranges per process and product: feedstock reheating (Table 2.6), intermediate heating, post-heating (Table 2.7), hot rolling (Table 2.8, electricity), cold rolling (Table 3.3), batch and continuous annealing, hot dip coating feedstock heating, batch galvanising (whole plant and kettle); the BAT-AEPLs for energy (Tables 9.1-9.4, 9.22, 9.24) as separate processes (they come from the same data collection, so they overlap the fleet ranges); technique examples with absolute energy figures: UK regenerative-burner retrofit (3.55 to 1.7 GJ/t), SSAB Raahe WBF 4/5 (Table 2.20), hot/direct charging (Table 2.23, Liberty Ostrava, Imatra), conventional vs thin slab reheating, annealing with recuperative burners / degreasing heat recovery / feedstock preheating, SSAB Borlänge HN vs 100 % H2 bell annealing (Table 8.2) and the 100 % H2 fleet range, induction vs gas wire heating efficiencies, NatSteel ORC (capex, capacity), Voestalpine waste heat boiler (capex, steam), soaking pit thermal input, and acid regeneration energy (Tables 3.10, 3.13, 3.15, 3.17, 3.18). The data-collection SEC is defined as heat plus electricity per t of feedstock processed (Sect. 9.4.4.1, Annex 11.6), so target is blank (total) except hot rolling (printed as electricity); Annex 11.6 converts fuels with net calorific values, so these rows are LHV. _measures.csv: percentage and absolute savings of furnace techniques (Sect. 2.4.2, 8.5). _flows.csv: N2/H2 for bell annealing, steam for acid evaporation, iron oxide from HCl spray roasting. _other-values.csv: furnace sizes, oxygen production electricity, thermal efficiencies, ORC savings, kettle losses, thin-film galvanising per m2, wire drawing SEC, JVD cost, NCV table. Not loaded: all non-GHG emissions (NOx, dust, acids, BAT-AEELs), water, materials, noise; plant-level figures shown only as charts (Figures 2.32-2.35, 3.17-3.19, 5.11, 6.4-6.6, 2.82, 2.96); Annex 11.6 virtual Plant A examples. No numbers found for electrolytic coating lines, coupled pickling-tandem mills, forging or whole pickling lines. Traps: cover/back says EUR 31321 EN (the task brief said EUR 31277); hot dip coating and annealing SEC cover the furnace only; the thin slab 0.50 GJ/t is the tunnel furnace only; BAT-AEPL tables mix batch and continuous annealing in one range; costs carry no price year.

(1) Text p.73 says MJ/t is per total amount of feedstock processed expressed in t/year (a unit slip; it is per t). (2) Table 2.8 layout is ambiguous: the 95-98 % reduction is printed on its own line between the carbon and high-alloy rows of strips and heavy plates; read as belonging to high-alloy steel. (3) Sect. 2.4.2.5 Shelby example: "65 % energy consumption is reported" read as a 65 % reduction. (4) Example-plant list in 2.4.2.6 repeats 242 HR. (5) Fig. 2.96 values only as bars.
